extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writers preparing and sending submissions/query letters to literary agents so the submission passes intern screening and is evaluated on writing quality rather than careless mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the agency’s guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission guidelines are posted on every agency’s website. Read them and follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't follow the agency's stated instructions you risk being tossed before anyone reads a word. This includes format, materials requested, and any special submission directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify agent availability and genre fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the agent you are querying still works at the agency, represents the genre you write, and can be found at the email address you are using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring this shows you didn't do research; double-check agent listings/contact info on the agency site before querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a killer query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: A query letter is an introduction to you and your writing; avoid vague, confusing, or poorly written queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the query concise and clear — it's too short for lengthy explanations. Use resources/examples if unsure. The query should introduce the book plainly for someone meeting it for the first time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confusing details that only make sense inside the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include confusing information in the query just because 'it makes sense in the book.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A query reader has not read the manuscript; anything unclear will mislead. Remedy: have someone who has never read the manuscript look at the query and point out misleading passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make submissions easy to read (put content in email body unless requested otherwise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the agency requests otherwise, post all content in the body of the email rather than sending links or attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send an email that only contains a link to a website that may redirect to poorly formatted pages with music or illegible colors (example: music and light-blue text on a burgundy background).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure contact information is clearly visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your contact information clearly in the submission so agents/interns can reach you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy to find email, phone, and any other required contact details rather than burying them or relying on linked pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not call to check submission status
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid calling the agency to check the status of your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calling is intrusive and unnecessary; follow the agency's stated response-time guidance instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit multiple manuscripts in a single query
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not query several manuscripts in a single submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents expect one project per query unless they request otherwise; sending multiple projects is confusing and unprofessional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread; avoid typos and grammar mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid typos and grammar mistakes — proofread your materials carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neat, error-free submissions increase your chance of getting a response. Sloppy submissions suggest carelessness and may be rejected before the writing is fairly evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust your writing — avoid gimmicks or extraneous materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the writing do the talking; do not clutter submissions with extra materials or props intended to get attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of bad extras: shredded newspaper, a pair of baby shoes, photos of your dog. Such additions usually make recipients uncomfortable and distract from the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make grandiose sales promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid statements like 'I guarantee this book will sell a million copies' or other larger-than-life claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not try to talk an agent into seeing how great the manuscript is; let the work and quality of writing demonstrate value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid irrelevant or misleading credentials and name-dropping
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present irrelevant credentials (e.g., a high-school paper essay) or name-drop agents/editors who don't know you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tactics are transparent and ineffective; credentials should be relevant and verifiable. Agents see through unwarranted claims or false associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize the writing above all else
rubrics_metrics.description: The writing is the most important part; everything else (credentials, gimmicks, lists of rejections) is just noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript and query communicate the strength of your writing rather than relying on packaging or extraneous materials to sell it.
